newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN OPEN FIVE-POINT LEAD AS DORTMUND SLUMP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN OPEN FIVE-POINT LEAD AS DORTMUND SLUMP.

text.p: Bayern Munich opened a big lead at the top of the German first division with a convincing 3-2 win over Cologne on Saturday while challengers Borussia Dortmund slumped to a 3-2 defeat at lowly Duisburg.
Two goals from Italian striker Ruggiero Rizzitelli and one from Juergen Klinsmann gave the Bavarians their fifth win in succession and put them five points clear with seven matches left.
Meanwhile European Cup semifinalists Dortmund, bidding for a third straight title, never looked like shrugging off a string of injuries and fell to fourth with the defeat to their local rivals.

VfB Stuttgart returned to their free-scoring ways with a 5-1 demolition of struggling Hansa Rostock, featuring goals from their "magic triangle" of Krasimir Balakov, Giovane Elber and Fredi Bobic, to move into third.

Bayern's nearest rivals after the weekend fixtures, Bayer Leverkusen, also kept their title hopes flickering with a 3-1 home victory over Karlsruhe on Friday. The win gave them 53 points to Bayern's 58, with both Stuttgart and Dortmund on 52.
Dortmund, already without their entire first-choice striking line-up, learned just before kickoff that they would have to do without playmaker Andreas Moeller, laid low with influenza.
Duisburg never looked in serious trouble after Marcus Marin made it 2-0 after 47 minutes. Togolese striker Bachirou Salou had given them the lead with just nine minutes gone.
Dortmund now face a crucial 10 days, entertaining Bayern next weekend and then travelling to Manchester United to defend a 1-0 first-leg lead in the European Cup.
"There are still 21 points up for grabs, so there's everything to play for," said trainer Ottmar Hitzfeld. "Today was a setback, so we have to beat Bayern."
But the Munich side have struck the kind of form that suggests they may be out of reach.
Rizzitelli twice pounced on loose balls in the goalmouth during a lethal 17-minute spell.

In between, Klinsmann showed how Bayern could overcome off-the-field squabbles by slamming home a dream pass from his opponent in the team power struggle, libero Lothar Matthaeus, to take his season's tally to 12.

But Cologne came within a whisker of spoiling the party as Bayern eased up, scoring twice in the last 11 minutes and forcing goalkeeper Oliver Kahn to full stretch with almost the last kick of the match, from Ion Vladoiu.

Stuttgart were left to rue inept draws against lowly opposition in the last two weeks as their goalscoring machine roared into life again, the 5-1 win against Rostock taking their tally to 66 from 27 games.

It took Germany striker Bobic just three minutes to score his 18th goal of the season. Attacking midfielder Balakov added two more in two minutes just after halftime and Brazilian Elber converted a Bobic pass in the 71st minute.
Marco Haber drove the ball in from 15 metres five minutes later, while Yasser Radwan scored Rostock's consolation goal three minutes from time.
